players.product: Large-scale liquid-cooled AI data-center campuses (Polaris Forge / Delta Forge)

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q2 2026 (quarter ended November 30, 2025): revenues were $126.6 million, up 250% from $36.2 million in the prior year, driven primarily by $73 million of tenant fit-out services revenue in the HPC Hosting Business plus $12 million of recognized revenue from the commencement of the first CoreWeave lease at Polaris Forge 1 (partial quarter; lease revenue on a cash basis was approximately $8 million, the gap reflecting ASC 842 straight-line accounting over 15 years). CFO: 'After two years of construction and over $1 billion invested in our first 100-megawatt data center, we have now begun to generate lease revenues.' The Data Center Hosting segment (286 megawatts of customer ASICs across two North Dakota facilities) contributed $41.6 million of revenue, up 15%, and roughly $16 million in segment operating profit on a $131 million asset base. Cost of revenues $100.6 million; SG&A $57 million versus $26 million (the increase included $23.8 million more stock-based comp from accelerated vesting); net loss $31.2 million or $0.11 per share; adjusted EBITDA $20.2 million.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $126.6 million, up 250%; tenant fit-out $73 million; Data Center Hosting $41.6 million, up 15%; adjusted EBITDA $20.2 million; net loss $31.2 million

quarterly_data.signal: Contracted HPC capacity after two hyperscale leases: Polaris Forge 1 will host 400 megawatts for CoreWeave (approximately $11 billion over approximately 15 years; remainder of the campus expected to be completed by the end of 2027), plus a roughly $5 billion 15-year lease with a U.S.-based investment-grade hyperscaler for 200 megawatts at Polaris Forge 2 (a $3 billion project near Harwood, North Dakota; initial capacity expected in 2026 and full build-out in 2027) - together 600 megawatts of lease capacity and approximately $16 billion in prospective lease revenue across the North Dakota campuses. CFO: lease revenues are expected to ramp over the next quarter; the two campuses under construction come online over calendar 2026 and 2027, with 'meaningful revenue growth over the coming 18 to 24 months', excluding campuses still in advanced discussions. CEO: next deliveries are the CoreWeave building in the middle part of this year, the Harwood building shortly after, then the next two buildings in Ellendale and Harwood.
quarterly_data.figure: 600 megawatts of lease capacity; approximately $16 billion in prospective lease revenue; Polaris Forge 2 200 megawatts, roughly $5 billion 15-year lease

capex.display: approximately $16 billion in prospective lease revenue
capex.metric: prospective lease revenue (Polaris Forge 1 + Polaris Forge 2)

quarterly_data.signal: Pipeline: having secured two hyperscale leases, inbound demand increased meaningfully; Applied Digital is in advanced discussions with another investment-grade hyperscaler across multiple regions (additional Dakotas locations and select Southern U.S. markets) - CEO: 'we're in advanced discussion on 3 sites in 900 megawatts', cautioning they could close one at a time, or none. It will start construction on at least one new campus by the end of January on high confidence of a lease with a new investment-grade hyperscaler different from the Harwood tenant (land and equipment already purchased with a new facility draw). Of the 6 targeted customers (the 5 investment-grade hyperscalers plus CoreWeave), it has completed onboarding with 5, which shortens the path to new contracts. The CEO agreed with an analyst's recap that 2026 deal volume could match or exceed 2025's (the analyst cited $16 billion of deals in '25 from a CNBC interview).
quarterly_data.figure: 3 sites in 900 megawatts in advanced discussion; onboarded with 5 of the 6 targeted customers

quarterly_data.signal: Long-term outlook: management now expects to surpass its long-term goal of $1 billion in NOI within 5 years. Every campus has the potential to reach at least a gigawatt; two current campuses can each go to 2 gigawatt or more, and three more campuses in advanced stage could each scale to 2 gigawatt capacity with different customers - if those contracts are put in place, a path to 5 gigawatts by 2030, 2031 or 2032; CEO: 'if we can expand to 5 campuses and have a clear path to 5 gigawatts plus of capacity over the next 5 years. That's a really great position'. CEO frames the market as 'extraordinary hyperscaler investment now exceeding $400 billion annually'.
quarterly_data.figure: surpass $1 billion in NOI within 5 years; 5 gigawatts plus of capacity over the next 5 years (if it can expand to 5 campuses)

quarterly_data.signal: Lease economics: CEO says pricing 'has been stable to slightly better over the past 6 months' and the demand profile 'extraordinarily robust'; contract terms have become more favorable - current leases are effectively noncancelable for 15 years (a customer cancelling for convenience owes the full 15 years of payments, a 100% make whole), and transferability is limited to a counterparty with an equal or higher credit rating.
quarterly_data.figure: pricing stable to slightly better over the past 6 months; noncancelable for 15 years; 100% make whole

quarterly_data.signal: Execution, not demand, is the limiter: the CEO says the constraint is how much Applied Digital can build across multiple sites 'from a supply chain perspective, from a personnel perspective, on an annualized basis' (a limit it says it has not hit yet). It secured supply chain 18 months plus ago, locking in '600, 700 megawatts of MEP per year', and is now working to expand that because it 'needs to go larger'. Lessons from the first CoreWeave building (delivered on time and on budget) led to fewer SKUs and suppliers under its fourth generation design; modular buildings with prefabricated components shorten construction timelines and are designed for different GPU and ASIC chip architectures and networking, supporting training, inference and traditional cloud workloads.
quarterly_data.figure: 600, 700 megawatts of MEP per year locked in

quarterly_data.signal: Power: a traditional natural gas turbine ordered today would probably not be delivered 'until 2031, 2032', so Applied Digital is working with utilities (starting in the Dakotas) and strategic partners including Babcock & Wilcox Enterprises to explore ways to add power to the grid without increasing costs to customers. The 'BW solution' uses steam turbines (coal-plant-style boilers) fired with natural gas, which the CEO says can bring generation forward '3, 4-plus years'; more information on a site and a build schedule for that equipment is expected in the first quarter. Management cites the Dakotas' low-cost abundant energy and natural cooling as a durable advantage.
quarterly_data.figure: gas turbine ordered today delivered 2031, 2032; BW solution 3, 4-plus years sooner

quarterly_data.signal: Liquid cooling: Applied Digital led and invested $15 million in a $25 million funding round for Corintis, whose patterned micro-channel cold plates are designed per chip (the CEO cites B200, B300, Rubin) and are intended to move inside the semiconductor packaging in the future. The CEO says the technology can use the same amount of liquid as chip power rises from 1 kilowatt to 3 kilowatts or 5 kilowatts (up to a point, after which more liquid is needed), helping Applied Digital future-proof its data-center infrastructure for chips with 3x the power density.
quarterly_data.figure: $15 million in a $25 million funding round for Corintis

quarterly_data.signal: Cloud spin-out: non-binding Letter of Intent to combine Applied Digital Cloud with EKSO Bionics to form ChronoScale, a dedicated GPU accelerated-compute platform built on a cloud platform 'among the first to deploy NVIDIA H100 GPUs at scale'. Closing is anticipated in the first half of 2026 (CEO: a definitive agreement hopefully later this month or early in February, then a shareholder vote to complete the merger; March at the very early side, but he expects the April-May time frame), after which Applied Digital expects to own over 80% of ChronoScale. The cloud business generates over $60 million in trailing 12-month revenue with $313 million in assets; the CEO says ChronoScale's key advantage will be access to Applied Digital's large-scale data-center facilities to deploy accelerated compute (GPUs, TPUs or LPUs).
quarterly_data.figure: over 80% ownership of ChronoScale; over $60 million trailing 12-month revenue; $313 million in assets

quarterly_data.signal: Financing framework: pre-leased construction is funded by the $100 million Macquarie Equipment Capital development loan facility (first draw made after quarter end); once an investment-grade hyperscaler lease is executed, Macquarie Asset Management's $5 billion preferred equity facility is tapped - $900 million drawn to date for Polaris Forge 1 and 2 - so third-party capital funds a majority of upfront investment while Applied Digital retains majority ownership of each site. The quarter closed a $2.35 billion private offering of 9.25% senior secured notes due 2030 to finance 2 of the 3 buildings at Polaris Forge 1 (goal: refinance at lower rates once operational; working to reduce the cost of debt for the third building). Quarter end: $2.3 billion in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash versus $2.6 billion in debt (most of which does not mature until 2030) and approximately $2.1 billion in total equity, excluding $382.5 million of financing proceeds completed after quarter end.
quarterly_data.figure: $2.35 billion 9.25% senior secured notes due 2030; $900 million drawn from $5 billion preferred equity facility; $2.3 billion cash vs $2.6 billion debt

connects_to.relationship: Polaris Forge 1 — 400 MW dedicated AI data-center campus leased to CoreWeave (North Dakota)

contracts.signal: Polaris Forge 1 reached ready-for-service, energizing 100 megawatts on schedule and completing the first of 3 contracted buildings; the rest of the campus is expected to be completed by the end of 2027 and will host 400 megawatts for CoreWeave, representing approximately $11 billion in prospective lease revenue over approximately 15 years. The fiscal Q2 included $12 million of recognized revenue from the commencement of the first CoreWeave lease (partial quarter). A $2.35 billion 9.25% senior secured notes offering finances 2 of the 3 buildings. The CEO expects to deliver the next CoreWeave building in the middle part of this year.
contracts.value: approximately $11 billion prospective lease revenue; $12 million recognized revenue in the quarter
